plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin for the DSH Mobile Android app: QR pairing, DSH on your phone, answer approvals from notifications.
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH Mobile — host plugin for DeepSeek Harness

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md)

`@kinocode/dsh-mobile` is a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin for the DSH Mobile Android app. It lets you:

- Pair your phone by scanning a QR code in the DSH sidebar.
- Use the regular DSH web UI on your phone through an HTTPS gateway running on your computer.
- On phones, let the session title use the available header width and tap it to see the full title. Only the session header reserves space for the floating navigation buttons.
- Answer approval requests and agent questions from notifications in the live desktop session (the first answer from any device wins).
- Receive a notification when a watched session finishes its turn.

The Android app is distributed separately and is not part of this repository. This is an unofficial project, not affiliated with DeepSeek.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`. The range is pinned because the plugin relies on internal DSH Gateway APIs that are not yet stable.
- The DSH web server (`webserver` service), included with DSH Desktop.
- Node.js 22.4 or later (the runtime bundled with DSH Desktop works).
- Phone and computer on the same network, or both on [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/).
- For notifications: a relay server (see [Notifications and the relay](#notifications-and-the-relay)).

## Install

Add `@kinocode/dsh-mobile` on the DSH Plugins page, or run:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @kinocode/dsh-mobile
```

Restart DSH. The log should show `[mobile-bridge] gateway listening {"origins":[...]}`.

## Pair a phone

1. Click **スマホを接続** ("Connect phone") at the bottom of the DSH sidebar.
2. In the app, tap **QR を読み取る** ("Scan QR") and scan the code. If you do not have a camera, use **リンクをコピー** ("Copy link") and paste the link into the app.
3. The code is single-use and expires after 5 minutes. Click **新しい QR** ("New QR") to generate another.

The panel also lists paired phones and lets you remove them. Removing a phone revokes its access immediately. The panel is currently available only in Japanese.

On the phone, the DSH sidebar is hidden so the conversation gets the full width. The round button at the top left opens it over the conversation; picking a session or tapping outside closes it. It reopens where you left the list, including the sessions shown with "さらに…件のセッションを表示" ("Show … more sessions"). Long-press a session and lift your finger to open its menu (pin, rename, fork, archive, copy session ID); this works even when a long title hides the row's buttons. Long-press and drag still reorders sessions as before. A closed project shows the most urgent state among its sessions with the same marks the sessions use (amber dot = waiting for an approval, review or answer, then spinner = running, then green dot = finished and not yet viewed). Desktop-only buttons are hidden.

When you add a workspace on the phone, the computer's folders are listed on the phone instead of opening a folder dialog on the computer. Browse to a folder or type its path, then tap **このフォルダを使う** ("Use this folder").

Settings also close with a left-to-right swipe (on the tab strip, the swipe scrolls the tabs instead).

A question from the AI keeps its options and the skip/send buttons on screen even when the question is long: the question text scrolls within about a quarter of the screen.

The right sidebar (files, preview, changes review, browser, terminal) opens full screen on the phone. Buttons that open an app or Finder on the computer are hidden on the phone; the file preview offers **スマホに保存** ("Save to phone") instead, which saves to the phone's Downloads. If the page stays blank after DSH restarts, it reloads by itself.

The round buttons at the top left (sidebar) and top right (right sidebar) can be moved anywhere: long-press one, then drag it.

In DSH's built-in browser (the right sidebar's Browser), words that are not an address are searched: Google on the desktop, Bing on the phone. The phone can only show pages that allow being framed (Google and others refuse), so ↗ (Open in system browser) opens the page in Chrome.

## Configuration

All fields are optional. Add them to your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. A profile patch replaces the plugin's entire configuration, so include every field you want to keep.

```yaml
- id: mobile-bridge
  config:
    relayUrl: https://relay.example.com
    relayEnrollToken: '...'
```

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `relayUrl` | `''` (off) | Relay used for notifications and answering from them. |
| `relayEnrollToken` | `''` | Token for a relay that only accepts known computers. |
| `gatewayEnabled` | `true` | Run the HTTPS gateway for phones. |
| `gatewayPort` | `3543` | Gateway port (1024–65535). |
| `gatewayHosts` | detected | IPv4 addresses to listen on. Only private addresses are accepted (see below). |
| `hostLabel` | computer name | Name shown on the phone. |
| `previewMaxChars` | `400` | Longest command preview shown in the app (50–4000). |
| `stateDir` | `$DSH_HOME/mobile-bridge` | Absolute path for host identity, paired devices, and certificates. `$DSH_HOME` defaults to `~/.dsh`. |

The configuration ID `mobile-bridge` and log name `dsh-mobile-bridge` are kept for compatibility with earlier versions.

## Phone history loading

Only the phone gateway limits opening history to 40 messages, targeting the latest 10 messages and one turn. Older history loads by itself when you scroll up to the top (once the scroll comes to rest, one page per swipe, keeping your place); the "さらに前の履歴を読み込む" ("Load earlier history") button stays as the loading indicator. Each older page brings at least 150 messages and 6 turns instead of stock DSH's 50 and 2. These budgets count user/assistant messages, not tool events or bytes. No DSH core or desktop changes are required.

An authenticated app-shell script saves opening snapshots in IndexedDB. Reopening the same host/device/session advertises verified SHA-256 record hashes; the gateway sends references for matching records and full data for misses. The browser reconstructs the authoritative snapshot before the stock client sees it. Cursor, projections, header, and assistant-stream baseline always come from the current server snapshot, never an optimistic cached replay. Reading the host's log still uses stock DSH; this optimization reduces phone transfer and initial history size, not host disk work.

Only records of at least 256 serialized UTF-8 bytes are advertised, with the hash property limited to 8KiB. If none qualify, no manifest is uploaded. Delta selection accounts for manifest upload as well as download savings. A complete cache miss can still incur the already-uploaded manifest overhead; total traffic is not guaranteed to shrink in every case.

Relay writes are serialized with source pause/resume while the destination drains. Buffered data exceeding 64MiB no longer causes termination. Stock WebSocket's 100MiB per-frame limit still applies; the message-count budget is not a byte limit.

The cache retains opening snapshots only, bounded globally to 12 sessions and 8MiB with a seven-day reuse expiry. Expired entries are removed during a later save/trim; physical deletion while the app is inactive is not guaranteed. It contains conversation text and tool results. On shared devices set `historyCacheEnabled: false` to stop persistence/reuse; this does not erase existing records. Clear the app/WebView's stored data in Android settings to erase them (pairing may need repeating). Revoking a device blocks connections and cache reuse, but does not remotely erase stored data. Storage denial falls back to online loading; a missing reference invalidates that cache entry and reconnects for a full snapshot. Storage is origin-specific, so changing LAN addresses causes a cold load; a stable Tailscale origin improves reuse.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `historyEnabled` | `true` | Optimize phone history; false restores stock transport. |
| `historyCacheEnabled` | `true` | Save/reuse device history independently of opening-page sizing. |
| `historyMaxMessages` | `40` | Opening cap, integer

plugins.description: A sidebar prompt template library for DeepSeek Harness: browse, manage, and insert reusable prompts into the composer.
plugins.readme_text:
# Prompt Library for DeepSeek Harness

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A DeepSeek Harness Web plugin that keeps reusable prompt templates one click away. It adds a searchable template library to the sidebar and a compact picker to the message composer. Choosing a template inserts it at the caret, or starts a new conversation with the template already in the draft when no conversation is open.

Repository: <https://github.com/qifenglun1/dsh-plugin-prompt>

## Features

- **Sidebar library** — a bookmark entry in the left sidebar opens a full library panel.
- **Composer picker** — a small bookmark button in the composer tool row opens a compact, searchable picker without leaving the conversation.
- **Insert at the caret** — templates are inserted into the current draft; a selection is replaced. The edit is undoable through the composer's normal undo history.
- **No-conversation fallback** — with no conversation open, choosing a template starts a new conversation and puts the template in the draft.
- **Template management** — create, edit, delete, duplicate, copy, search, and filter templates by category.
- **Categories** — create a category before it has templates. The empty category offers **New template in this category**. A name matching a built-in category label belongs to that built-in category instead of creating a duplicate.
- **Eight built-in templates** — code review, refactoring, tests, debugging, explanation, summarization, translation, and structured research. They follow the UI language and are read-only; **Save as mine** creates an editable copy.
- **English and Simplified Chinese UI** — the interface follows the DSH language setting.
- **No configuration required** — no API key, token, password, account, or external service.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2** or newer, with the Web or Desktop UI.
- A DSH profile in which bundles can be installed (the default Desktop profile is fine).
- Network access to GitHub when installing from this repository.

The plugin is a **bundle**, not a standalone web page. Install it through DSH's plugin manager; do not try to open `client.js` directly.

The repository root is the installable package root. It contains `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml`, `index.js`, and `client.js`; there is no monorepo subdirectory and no build step.

## Install from GitHub

### Desktop / Web (recommended)

1. In DSH, open **Plugins**.
2. Choose **Add plugin** → **Install a third-party plugin**.
3. Paste the repository address:

   ```text
   https://github.com/qifenglun1/dsh-plugin-prompt
   ```

4. Review the trust notice and confirm the installation. DSH reads `package.json` and installs the bundle.
5. If the `prompt-library` row remains off, enable it in **Plugins**.
6. If the sidebar bookmark does not appear, refresh the Web GUI once.

### CLI

`dsh plugin --profile <name> add ...` forwards the install to pnpm in that profile. Use the profile you actually run (`web`, `desktop`, or a custom profile):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:qifenglun1/dsh-plugin-prompt
```

The equivalent GitHub URL form is accepted by pnpm-based installs:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/qifenglun1/dsh-plugin-prompt
```

A git install fetches sources, not a prebuilt artifact. This package is plain JavaScript with no `prepare`/`build` script, so pnpm does not need to run an install-time build and users are not asked to allow one.

Do not edit the profile's `package.json` or `cordis.patch.yml` by hand; the plugin manager owns those files.

### Local checkout (development)

Install the absolute path to this repository as a linked bundle:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile dev add /absolute/path/to/dsh-plugin-prompt
```

The plugin manager links the checkout into the profile, so edits to `client.js` are picked up after a page refresh. Replace `dev` with a disposable profile name; do not mix development links into a profile you rely on.

### Update and uninstall

DSH upgrades non-official plugins by uninstalling and reinstalling them. Uninstall the bundle in **Plugins**, then install the new repository version. With the CLI:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-plugin-prompt
dsh plugin --profile web add github:qifenglun1/dsh-plugin-prompt
```

Removing the bundle removes the sidebar entry and composer picker. Templates already saved in the browser are not deleted by uninstalling; clear the keys below if you want to remove them.

## Configuration

The plugin has **no Config schema** and no required settings. There is no API key, token, password, endpoint, or model selection to configure.

| Setting | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Templates | Managed in the library panel or the template editor. |
| Categories | Created with **New category** or by typing a new category in the template editor. |
| Language | Follows the DSH language setting (`English` or `简体中文`). |
| Built-in templates | Fixed in the plugin; **Save as mine** creates an editable copy. |

### Browser storage

Templates and categories are stored in the Harness Web origin's `localStorage`:

- `dsh.prompt-library.templates.v1` — user templates.
- `dsh.prompt-library.categories.v1` — categories that exist independently of templates. When this key is missing, categories already used by saved templates are migrated into it.

`localStorage` is scoped to the Web origin. A different origin, browser profile, or cleared browser storage has separate data. The plugin does not write templates to the session log, does not send them to a server, and does not read credentials. When you send a message, its text reaches your configured model through DSH as usual.

## Usage

### Sidebar library

1. Click the bookmark entry in the left sidebar.
2. Search by title, text, or category, or choose a category chip.
3. Choose **Insert** to put the template into the current draft, **Copy** to copy it, or **Save as mine** to duplicate a built-in template.
4. Use **New category** to create a category before it has templates.
5. Use the back arrow in the panel header to return to the conversation.

### Composer picker

1. Click the bookmark button in the composer's left tool row.
2. In a new, empty conversation the picker opens as a centered dialog, so the search field is always visible; in an active conversation it opens above the composer.
3. Search for a template. Use the arrow keys to move and Enter to insert, or click a row.
4. The template is inserted at the caret (or replaces the current selection).

### Example

Create a reusable review prompt:

1. Open the sidebar library.
2. Choose **New template**.
3. Set the title to `Review a pull request`, the category to `Engineering`, and the body to:

   ```text
   Review this change for correctness, edge cases, performance, security,
   and maintainability. List issues by severity, then give concrete fixes.

   ```

4. Save. The template appears under **My templates**.
5. In any conversation, click the composer bookmark, choose the template, and it is inserted at the caret.

### Empty categories

A newly created category is selected immediately. Until it has templates, the panel shows **No templates in this category yet** and **New template in this category**. That button opens the editor with the category prefilled.

Categories can be created and selected, but renaming or deleting a category is not yet supported.

## Compatibility

- Built and verified with **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2**.
- The package declares `engines.dsh: ">=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0"`. Installation and profile startup refuse a bundle outside that range.
- The client half uses the public slot entries `sidebar.panellist`, `main`, `conversation.input.left`, and `conversation.input.overlay`, plus the composer's `InputActions.captureInsertion()` / `insertText()`.
- If a future DSH release changes those slots, the plugin may need an update. Please include the DSH version in bug reports.

## Privacy and security

- No analytics, telemetry, or network calls of its own.
- No credential, API key, token, cookie, or account access.
- No host filesystem access; the host half is an empty `apply()` row.
- Only templates and category names are stored, in this
